speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs whether the Government is working with the Malaysian authorities to facilitate Singaporeans entering Malaysia for essential personal matters such as family bereavements.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, in the last one year, the enforced separation by the border closures has had a profound emotional impact on many families in Singapore, especially when confronted by family bereavement.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: I have lost count of the number of emails I have received from people who were deprived of that opportunity to be with a family member at the end of life.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, we particularly sympathise and understand the feelings of Singaporeans and, indeed, Malaysians who are caught in such circumstances.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Having said that, we also fully understand the need for public health precautions, of which border closures are part.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: And we also recognise that it is the responsibility of each government to do whatever it takes in order to protect public health.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Throughout this epidemic, we have been in close contact with the Malaysian authorities and we have worked with them to facilitate travel for Singaporeans with essential or compassionate reasons for travel.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: As Members of the House are aware, the COVID-19 situation keeps evolving very rapidly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Even our previously agreed Reciprocal Green Lanes and travel bubbles have had to be opened and shut, sometimes quite quickly.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: So, I hope all Members understand that this is a dynamic and difficult situation.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We are doing our best but, from time to time, we will sometimes have to take tough decisions.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister for Foreign Affairs.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: First, in his earlier reply, he mentioned that the Ministry has facilitated successfully about 250 appeals for travel by Singaporeans and PRs across the Causeway.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I have some residents who were obviously not successful in their attempts to get across and this was despite MFA Consular officers coming in to try to assist, but there was just no response from the Malaysian side.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: So, I would like to ask how can the Ministry take this forward to ensure that there is a broader baseline or more objectivity to facilitate such travel, such that it is not just hit-and-miss where some appeals are allowed and some are not, and I do not know the circumstances of the 250 successful appeals.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: The second question, perhaps more broadly, is that we are all aware of the dynamic political situation in Malaysia and also the state of emergency currently.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, the majority of cases did not get through.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I am not in a position to say on what basis he agreed to some of our requests and disagreed with many of the other requests.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I would also say that I have also come across many cases, when the Singaporean is made aware of how difficult the hurdles are in place, they have sometimes decided that because of the lack of time, that it would be pointless to try to get across the Causeway and to delay the funeral.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, all in all, it has been a very tough, a very heart-wrenching time for these families.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: And what I can assure is that MFA takes seriously each and every single case.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: On Ms Sylvia Lim's second point about what she described as the dynamic political situation in Malaysia, the state of emergency and the rest of it, what I would say from an MFA perspective is that throughout this entire crisis – and Members must remember, in the case of Malaysia, they have even gone through a change of government in the past one year – nevertheless, throughout this crisis, we have been able to maintain good functional communications and relations between the Prime Ministers, between the Ministers, certainly between myself and the Foreign Minister of Malaysia Dato' Sri Hishammuddin Hussein, and as well as at the public service, civil service level.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, the point is, on both sides of the Causeway, we are dealing with a very difficult situation.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: My objective is to keep relations open, keep communications honest, constructive, helpful.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: Not to make things worse, not to put undue pressure which would actually cause damage to the long-term challenge of both countries having to deal with this pandemic.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, all in all I would say that our relations remain in a very good state.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I am sorry that we have not been able to persuade the authorities in Malaysia to agree to every request that has come from Singaporeans, but we will do our best.
